text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- A joint report by the ministries of justice, foreign and interior affairs said the Foreign Ministry intervened in police procedures on behalf of alleged Iranian murderers of three Kurdish leaders in 1989. However the 130-page report is contradictory in parts.

- Civil servants in the Finance Ministry will hold a 12-hour warning-strike on June 3 in order to protest against the government's austerity measures in the public sector. The demands by the labour union would cost six billion schillings.
- A report by Roland Berger says Unifrost, a unit of Unilever, should halve the number of its employees at its Austrian production plant to 542. This could create savings of 400 million schillings.
- Agriculture Minister supports the milk industry's plan to raise milk prices.

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger says current central bank director Adolf Wala will be Austria's representative with the European Central Bank, and not Austria's central bank president Klaus Liebscher.
- Edlinger sees no urgent demand for the government to sell its stake in Bank Austria within the year.

- Vienna's Finance councillor Brigitte Ederer wants to change the savings banks' law in order to reduce the City of Vienna's influence in Bank Austria. The opposition Greens say the power of Bank Austria is too great.
- Kontrollbank will keep its dividend at 45 schillings even though profits went down slightly.
- Bank Burgenland's operating profits more than doubled by 103 percent to 70.9 million schillings in 1996.
DIE PRESSE
- The government coalition agrees there was no political pressure in the affair surrounding the release of the suspected murderers of the Kurdish leaders.
- One billion schillings from the sale of the government's stake in Creditanstalt will be ready to subsidise research projects by June.

- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner sees the race for postal savings bank PSK as already over. He expects insurers Wiener Staedtische and BARC to take over the government's 49-percent stake in the bank.
- Chemicals group Krems Chemie has taken over the paper chemicals unit from Furtenbach in order to strengthen its market position.
- The Republic of Austria counld be made liable for loans worth 104 billion schillings by the Kontrollbank.

- Car drivers paid 2.1 billion schillings in motorway fees in the first quarter of 1997. Around 1.3 billion schillings of the earnings have to be used for the completion of Austria's motorway network.
- Creditanstalt says it plans further acquisitions in eastern Europe after it has opened a subsidiary in Danzig, Poland.
KURIER
- Die Erste savings bank plans a capital increase of six to eight billion schillings in order to pay for its takeover of GiroCredit.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Chamber of Economy vice-president Alfons Haiden says Italy should be in the first round of countries to join the European Economic and Monetary Union even if it does not meet the criteria exactly.
